title: Advanced Idioms for Business
completion_message: ¡Formidable! Los 'Idioms' avanzados son la marca definitiva de la fluidez nativa en el mundo corporativo. Usar expresiones como 'cash cow' o 'corner the market' te permite sonar natural, persuasivo y completamente integrado en la cultura de negocios anglosajona.

parts.visual:
Idioms de Inicio y Éxito: 
- Get off the ground (Empezar a funcionar o tener éxito / Despegar). 
Ej: It's hard to get a new business off the ground. 
- Corner the market (Acaparar el mercado / Dominar un sector). 
Ej: Amazon has cornered the market in online retail. 
- Cash cow (Vaca lechera / Producto o división que genera ganancias constantes y seguras sin mucha inversión). 
Ej: The software subscription is the company's cash cow.
parts.audio: Business Idioms for Starting and Success. 'Get off the ground' means to start functioning successfully. For example: It's hard to get a new business off the ground. 'Corner the market' means to dominate a particular sector or area of business. For example: Amazon has cornered the market in online retail. A 'Cash cow' is a product or service that generates a steady return of profits. For example: The software subscription is the company's cash cow.

parts.visual:
Idioms de Dificultad y Negociación: 
- Cut corners (Acortar camino / Hacer algo mal o de forma barata para ahorrar tiempo o dinero). 
Ej: We cannot afford to cut corners on safety. 
- Play hardball (Jugar duro / Ser implacable y agresivo en una negociación). 
Ej: The unions are playing hardball over the new contracts. 
- Red tape (Cinta roja / Burocracia excesiva y trámites). 
Ej: Opening a branch in that country involves too much red tape.
parts.audio: Idioms for Difficulty and Negotiation. To 'Cut corners' means to do something perfunctorily so as to save time or money, often sacrificing quality or safety. For example: We cannot afford to cut corners on safety. To 'Play hardball' means to act aggressively or ruthlessly, especially in politics or business negotiations. For example: The unions are playing hardball over the new contracts. 'Red tape' refers to excessive bureaucracy or adherence to official rules and formalities. For example: Opening a branch in that country involves too much red tape.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el idiom de negocios correcto.

questions.question: We need more funding to get this project off the ____. (Despegar / Empezar a funcionar).
questions.explanation: Get off the ground = despegar, iniciar con éxito.

questions.question: With their new algorithm, they have managed to ____ the market in digital advertising. (Acaparar).
questions.explanation: Corner the market = acaparar el mercado.

questions.question: The printer division has been our ____ cow for the last ten years. (Fuente segura de ingresos).
questions.explanation: Cash cow = vaca lechera (producto muy rentable).

questions.question: If we want to maintain our quality standards, we cannot afford to ____ corners. (Ahorrar a costa de calidad).
questions.explanation: Cut corners = hacer algo de la forma más rápida y barata, saltando reglas.

questions.question: During the negotiations, the other company decided to play ____ and refused to compromise. (Jugar duro/agresivo).
questions.explanation: Play hardball = actuar agresivamente sin ceder.

questions.question: It took months to get the permits because of all the government ____ tape. (Burocracia).
Since the CEO resigned, the company has been going down the ____. (Irse a pique / Fracasar).
questions.explanation: Go down the drain = desperdiciarse, irse a la basura.

questions.question: We need to think outside the ____ to solve this unprecedented problem. (Pensar de forma creativa).
questions.explanation: Think outside the box = pensar con originalidad.

questions.question: I don't know the exact figures, but as a ____ park estimate, I'd say $50,000. (Cálculo aproximado).
Before we sign the contract, let's make sure we are all on the same ____. (Estar de acuerdo / En la misma onda).
questions.explanation: On the same page = tener el mismo entendimiento.

questions.question: They offered me a job, but there are some strings ____. (Condiciones ocultas).
questions.explanation: Strings attached = con condiciones o ataduras.

questions.question: The new regulations will be a tough ____ to swallow for the industry. (Algo difícil de aceptar).
questions.explanation: A tough/bitter pill to swallow = algo desagradable que hay que aceptar.

questions.question: We've been working on this for 12 hours. Let's call it a ____. (Dar por terminado el trabajo por hoy).
questions.explanation: Call it a day = terminar de trabajar por hoy.

questions.question: Our competitor's new product really threw a ____ in the works. (Causar un problema en un plan).
questions.explanation: Throw a spanner (UK) / monkey wrench (US) in the works = arruinar o estorbar un plan.

questions.question: We need to get everyone up to ____ on the new compliance rules before Friday. (Poner al día).
questions.explanation: Get up to speed = actualizarse, informarse bien de algo.

questions.question: We are losing money every month; we are operating in the ____. (En números rojos / Con pérdidas).
questions.explanation: In the red = perdiendo dinero. In the black = dando beneficios.

questions.question: The manager decided to bite the ____ and fire the toxic employee. (Afrontar una situación difícil).
questions.explanation: Bite the bullet = afrontar algo difícil e inevitable.

questions.question: Learning this new software is a steep learning ____. (Curva de aprendizaje pronunciada/difícil).
questions.explanation: Steep learning curve = difícil de aprender rápido.

questions.question: I'm overwhelmed with work right now; my plate is completely ____. (Tener mucho trabajo).
questions.explanation: Have a full plate = estar muy ocupado.

questions.question: Let's touch ____ next week to review the progress. (Contactar brevemente).
questions.explanation: Touch base = contactarse brevemente para actualizarse.
